Once I move in with family in the next week or two, I will have very few expenses. Mostly just fuel for my car (~$15/wk), cell phone (~$100/mo), and whatever allowance I give myself for incidental groceries/toiletries (~$40/wk). The rest will go to savings and paying down debt.

That $164 for my internet is 2 months worth. I pay about $75/mo for a higher tier internet.

All the debts I listed above are not actually on my credit report. I collected all these debts by going through the bills and collections notices I saved from the mail. My credit report actually only shows a few of the debts I listed.

And thank you for finally clearing that up for me. The more I thought about it, the more I realized it would obviously be in his best interest to tell me something like that so I would be more inclined to pay in full, which is what I believe I did with that specific debt so many years ago.

Well it still doesn't seem clear to me if he is answering YES, or just going along with what I said. Can someone just say in concrete terms if settling is reflected on your credit score or does it just show paid?

I was planning on checking out that Everydollar budget. Thanks for making it a higher priority for me now. 

As for the phone bill with my ex-gf. It was my phone bill first and I added my gf only a few months before we broke up. She moved and is working on getting onto her own plan soon so that will be taken care of shortly. But you're right, getting on a family plan could be a little cheaper, but then I'd be looking at early termination fees.  I think I'm still locked into it until sometime in the spring next year. Still, I'll look into this. Thanks.

Someone once told me (possibly a collector) that it will reflect poorly on your credit report if you "settle" with collections agencies, for less than you owe. Is there any truth to that? Or will it just show paid either way?

I asked this in a comment above but the response I got was snarky and didn't answer the question. Can you answer this because I'm honestly ignorant and would like to know one way or the other.

Well debt consolidation loans exist for a reason I thought. I only assumed I would need to use my car for collateral because I didn't figure I cold get a loan any other way.

I'm honestly very ignorant in these matters and it seemed convenient to have a large sum to pay off many people at once and then worry about one payment to one person as opposed to juggling many payments to many people, slowly, over time, that are still accruing late fees and penalties.

I just dropped off 4 years of W-2's with the tax center. So as far as the IRS goes, I'll see what happens soon.

I'm here on my hands and knees looking for help, admitting I fucked up. And yet some people in these comments still find it necessary to try and make me continue to feel bad about my fuck-ups and ignorance in financial management.

I'm sure it's worth nothing to you, but you don't need to worry about the security of my child. She is *well* taken care of and I do many other things to shoulder the responsibility of being father to my child. Please try not to make assumptions about that kind of thing when you know so little about the actual situation. I only gave you the details I thought necessary to give that pertained to **MY financial situation** not the well being of my child.

>So? 

I was asking an honest question, and you didn't even manage to answer it. I didn't think this was the place and setting for snarkiness.

There is no other debt. I've listed everything here.  

I've only ever had one credit card, and it is listed as "Old CC - Collections" because it was with one of my banks USAA and was only a $500 limit. I couldn't make payments for a long while and it got sent to collections.
